processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Sample heated to 1200 °C at a rate of 10 °C/s.
Homogenized by holding at 1200 °C for 120 s.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set test temperature of 1000 °C at 5 °C/s.
Held at the set temperature (1000 °C) for 15 s before compression so the temperature inside and outside the sample was the same.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: 60% (corresponding to a maximum true strain of 0.92)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Isothermal constant-strain-rate compression carried out on the Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator at the set temperature of 1000 °C and strain rate 0.01 s⁻¹, to a maximum compression of 60% (true strain 0.92). Mica foils with high-temperature lubricants were affixed to the two end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity.
After compression the sample was sprayed with water to cool the steel down.

structures.overall_structure: Initial (pre-deformation) microstructure of the forged billet: large polygonal grains delimited by bright, continuous, slightly etched boundaries, enclosing dark grey grain interiors; within essentially every grain the interior carries many fine, closely spaced, parallel light-grey striations/lamellae whose direction changes from grain to grain, giving a strongly banded dendritic/interdendritic segregation contrast rather than a uniform solid solution.

After 60% hot compression (true strain 0.92) the cylindrical specimen develops three deformation zones (1 = difficult deformation zone, 2 = small deformation zone, 3 = large deformation zone); the degree of dynamic recrystallization is zone 3 > zone 2 > zone 1. For this sample's condition, which lies within the 950–1000 °C / 0.01–0.1 s⁻¹ regime regarded as giving sufficient DRX, the recrystallized grain structure is relatively fine and uniform; with decreasing strain rate the recrystallized grains grow and heterogeneity improves.

microstructure_list.region: large deformation zone (zone 3, core of the compressed sample)

defects.type: dislocations (work hardening / dynamic recovery) - rate dependent

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator; isothermal constant-strain-rate compression to 60% (true strain 0.92); mica foil + high-temperature lubricant at the end faces; water-spray quenched after compression

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Test matrix T = 900–1150 °C and ε̇ = 0.01–10 s⁻¹; examined condition T = 1000 °C, ε̇ = 0.01 s⁻¹; maximum compression 60% (true strain 0.92)
characterization_methods.purpose: Acquire flow (rheological) stress curves and study hot deformation and dynamic recrystallization behavior
characterization_methods.key_findings: The steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material; at ε̇ = 0.01 s⁻¹ peak stress drops from 305.4 MPa at 900 °C to 53.8 MPa at 1150 °C (82% reduction).

characterization_methods.technique: Optical metallography by laser confocal microscopy (after splitting, grinding, polishing and etching)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: LEXT OLS4000 laser confocal microscope; etchant = 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed sample split in half along the axial axis; prepared, ground, polished and etched; zones 1–3 examined with a 100 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the initial and hot-deformed microstructure and measure the DRX average grain size in the large-deformation (core) zone
characterization_methods.key_findings: Grain size is measured from the core (large deformation zone); DRX grain size increases with decreasing ε̇ or increasing T.

computational_details.simulation_method: Constitutive analysis with the Arrhenius hyperbolic-sine equation and the Zener–Hollomon (Z) parameter
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Linear-fit slopes k1 = 5.135 (lnε̇ vs ln[sinh(ασp)], Fig. 4a) and k2 = 15.690 (ln[sinh(ασp)] vs 1000/T, Fig. 4b); the fitted lines are not parallel, so Qp is an average over the experimental range.

analytical_models.equation_role: Relate peak stress σp, temperature T and strain rate ε̇ to determine the dynamic recrystallization activation energy Qp
analytical_models.model_note: α = β/n1 = 0.00599; Qp = 1000·R·k1·k2 (Eq. 2) = 669.844 kJ mol⁻¹. This is a material-level average over 900–1150 °C / 0.01–10 s⁻¹, not unique to this sample.

analytical_models.equation_role: Characterize the combined influence of T and ε̇ on flow stress: Z = ε̇·exp(Qp/RT)
analytical_models.model_note: For this sample's condition (1000 °C, 0.01 s⁻¹) lnZ = 58.69 (Table 1).

computational_details.simulation_method: Multiple linear regression of DRX characteristic values against lnZ; critical strain from the Cingara–McQueen equation with the Poliak–Jonas inflection-point (θ–σ) criterion
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Correlation coefficients: σc R = 0.947, εc R = 0.911; σp R = 0.957, εp R = 0.911; σs R = 0.956, εs R = 0.922

analytical_models.equation_role: Predict critical, peak and steady-state strains/stresses from lnZ
analytical_models.model_note: Global models for the steel; Cingara–McQueen material constant C = 0.1461 (R = 0.9728) determined at 1050 °C/0.01 s⁻¹ and εc/εp ≈ 0.452.

computational_details.simulation_method: DRX average grain-size prediction model regressed by the Levenberg–Marquardt optimization algorithm, for finite-element simulation
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Billet set as a rigid-plastic body and die indenter as a rigid body; semi-symmetric specimen used; shear-type friction at the billet–die interface = 0.3; billet–air convection coefficient = 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Correlation coefficient R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53%; absolute error generally below 3 µm

analytical_models.model_name: DRX average grain size prediction model (Eq. 12)
analytical_models.equation_role: Predict DRX average grain size d_rex from strain rate ε̇ and temperature T
analytical_models.model_note: General form d_rex = a·d0^h·ε^p·ε̇^q·exp(Q/RT)+b (Eq. 11); validated with R = 0.996, MRE = 4.53%.

unmapped_findings: Zener–Hollomon parameter at the sample condition (T = 1000 °C, ε̇ = 0.01 s⁻¹) is lnZ = 58.69 (Table 1).

For the ε̇ = 0.01 s⁻¹ series the peak stress decreases from 305.4 MPa at 900 °C to 53.8 MPa at 1150 °C (a reduction of 82%); the value specific to 1000 °C is not tabulated (only the 900 and 1150 °C endpoints are given).

The steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material: rheological stress increases with increasing ε̇ or decreasing T; peak stress can be lowered by decreasing ε̇ or increasing T (applicable to this condition).
This sample's condition (1000 °C, 0.01 s⁻¹) falls within the regime (950–1000 °C / 0.01–0.1 s⁻¹) considered to yield a refined, uniform recrystallized grain structure.

The paper reports no sample-specific DRX average grain-size number for 1000 °C/0.01 s⁻¹; Fig. 10 only shows that the 0.01 s⁻¹ curve reaches just below 80 µm at 1150 °C and that at 900 °C all strain-rate curves lie between roughly 8 and 13 µm.
The same Fe-Mn-Al-C steel batch and composition were used to confirm reproducibility of the observed phenomena under identical experimental conditions.
